title: What is El Niño?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What does El Niño do to the weather?
What is the difference between El Niño and La Niña?
Why is it called El Niño?

explain.say: El Niño is a natural change in the tropical Pacific Ocean that happens every two to seven years and shifts weather around the world. To see it, start with a normal year.

explain.say: Normally the trade winds blow from east to west across the Pacific, piling warm surface water up near Indonesia and Australia and bringing them rain. Off Peru, cold, nutrient-rich water rises up, feeding huge shoals of fish.

faq.a: El Niño is Spanish for the little boy, referring to the Christ child, because Peruvian fishermen noticed the warm water arriving around Christmas.
asks: Why is it called El Niño?

faq.a: La Niña, the little girl, is the opposite of El Niño. The trade winds blow harder than usual, the eastern Pacific gets colder, and the weather changes swing the other way.
asks: What is the opposite of El Niño?

faq.q: How does El Niño affect the weather?
faq.a: It moves where the tropical Pacific's warmest water and heaviest rain are, which shifts storm tracks worldwide. It can bring floods to Peru, droughts to Australia and India, and milder winters to parts of North America.

faq.q: Why does El Niño hurt fishing in Peru?
faq.a: Normally cold, nutrient-rich water wells up off Peru and feeds plankton and huge shoals of anchovies. In El Niño warm water covers it, the upwelling weakens, and the fish move away or die.
asks: What happens to fish in El Niño?

faq.q: Does El Niño make the world hotter?
faq.a: Yes, for a while. The Pacific releases heat into the air, so global temperatures usually rise a little during and just after a strong El Niño. It is a natural cycle, separate from long-term global warming.
asks: Is El Niño the same as global warming?

facts: El Niño events happen irregularly, about every two to seven years.
The strong El Niño of 2023 to 2024 helped make 2024 the warmest year on record at the time.

quiz.say: What happens to the Pacific trade winds during El Niño?
quiz.show: During El Niño the trade winds…
quiz.why: Weaker trade winds let the warm water that usually piles up in the west spread back east.

wrong.1: Extra-strong trade winds are a sign of La Niña, the opposite pattern.
wrong.2: El Niño lasts months to about a year, and then the winds return to normal.
